sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real decision, and how many validator hours are actually available?
criteria: Derives free MRM capacity: 12,600 − 12,100 = 500 hours
Applies the policy that bank validators do at least half of each validation, so 500 bank-led hours cover at most 1,000 total
Shows that validating all six from scratch (1,800 hours, 900 bank-led) does not fit
Protects the exam-finding work first and states something out of scope

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers the head of MRM, the model risk committee, the board, compliance and the business owners, each with a distinct want
Lets MRM scope its own platform validation rather than accept the first line's evidence plan
Includes examiners and what they will look for
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the sign-off options, and how many use cases fit in the free hours under each?
criteria: Includes an option that exempts generative AI and one that waits for the finding to close
Computes bank-led hours for each option against 500
Shows the platform-plus-tiers option fits five use cases (450 bank-led hours) and not the sixth
Chooses what to defer by value per validator hour and sensitivity, not by which business shouts loudest

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would change it?
criteria: Makes one recommendation in which the model risk committee, not the first line, rules on what is a model
Names the deferred use case and its value
Says what is reversible, such as moving a use case to a higher tier
Gives triggers, including the overdue-validation count and a filled requisition

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What value does each option deliver over three years, and what does it cost?
criteria: Compares three-year value with launch months labelled as assumptions
Prices contractor hours as new spend and separates first-line hours already on payroll
States model API spend and why it does not separate the options
Prices the deferral per month

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Where is the line between the first line and MRM, and who decides what?
criteria: Keeps validation conclusions with MRM and evidence with the first line
Names a business owner per use case
Gives compliance ownership of fair-treatment testing
Rejects a joint first-line and MRM validation team

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: In what order do the validations run, and where are the gates?
criteria: Validates the platform before any use case
Runs income extraction in parallel before it affects a credit decision
Has gates with measurable conditions
Puts the finding's closure in the plan ahead of the deferred use case

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong in a credit decision, and how are model changes handled?
criteria: Tests income extraction errors across applicant segments
Defines a change-validation path for provider model-version changes and fits its hours in the budget
Measures human review rather than assuming it works
Pauses generative AI validation if the overdue count slips

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the process works, and what would it hide?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Uses the overdue-validation count as a guard on generative AI progress
Tracks the largest accuracy gap between applicant segments
Sets cycle-time targets per tier

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and how often?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences, including the model risk committee and the board
Leads updates with the finding's status
Sets a monthly and a quarterly cadence
Avoids promising business owners dates before tier rulings
